node.label: J. R. Miller
node.date_label: Skyscrapers Hide the Heavens (1989) · Shingwauk’s Vision (1996) · Compact, Contract, Covenant (2009)
node.description: A settler historian of Indigenous–newcomer relations, residential schooling and treaties in Canada. Skyscrapers Hide the Heavens (1989) is his history of Indian–white relations in Canada. Shingwauk’s Vision (1996), a cross-Canada history of residential schooling, shifts the focus of responsibility from the churches toward the federal government and, ultimately, Euro-Canadian society. Celia Haig-Brown’s review credits the book’s breadth and research while criticizing how examples drawn across places and decades flatten differences among nations and schools, and questioning its claims to balance and its treatment of resistance. Compact, Contract, Covenant (2009) carries his work into the history of treaty-making.
